# SWAT 2012 Template

`version: swat` is the template for **SWAT 2012** projects. It lets you write a compact, SWAT-aware configuration — you don't need to specify every fixed-width column position and text-file row offset by hand. HydroPilot expands the template into a standard `version: general` config before execution.

This document covers SWAT 2012. For SWAT+, see the [SWAT+ template](swatplus.md).

## What the template expands into

| Aspect | Template input | Expanded general output |
|---|---|---|
| Writer type | implicit (SWAT knowledge) | `writerType: fixed_width` |
| Reader type | implicit (SWAT knowledge) | `readerType: text` |
| Parameter locations | variable name + HRU filter | concrete line/start/width/precision per file |
| Series rows | `id` + `period` + `timestep` | calculated `rowRanges` |
| Series columns | `variable` name | resolved `colSpan` from SWAT variable database |

The template expansion happens inside `SwatTemplate.build_config()`. The runtime always executes against the expanded `version: general` config. You can inspect the result by loading the config — HydroPilot writes `<stem>_general.yaml` next to the source YAML.

## Configuration shape

### `version`

```yaml
version: swat
```

### `basic`

Same fields as general mode. The template uses `projectPath` to discover SWAT project structure.

```yaml
basic:
  projectPath: E:\BMPs\TxtInOut
  workPath: ./work
  command: swat.exe
```

### `parameters`

Two-layer design:

- `design` — variables the optimizer sees (name, bounds, optional type).
- `physical` — how those variables are written into SWAT input files.

```yaml
parameters:
  design:
    - name: CN2
      bounds: [35, 98]
    - name: ALPHA_BF
      bounds: [0, 1]
    - name: GW_DELAY
      bounds: [0, 500]

  physical:
    - name: CN2
      mode: v
    - name: ALPHA_BF
      mode: v
    - name: GW_DELAY
      mode: v
```

When `physical` entries are omitted, the template fills defaults from the SWAT parameter database (file positions, widths, and precision).

#### HRU filtering

You can narrow which HRUs a parameter applies to with a `filter` block:

```yaml
physical:
  - name: CN2
    mode: v
    filter:
      subbasin: [1, 3, 5]
      land_use: AGRL
      soil: "Haplic Luvisols"
```

Filter rules:

- Same field, multiple values → OR (`subbasin: [1, 3, 5]` matches 1, 3, or 5).
- Different fields → AND (land_use + soil must both match).
- `not` block → exclude matching HRUs.
- No filter → applies to all HRUs.

```yaml
filter:
  land_use: AGRL
  not:
    slope: "30-45"
```

#### Discrete parameters

```yaml
design:
  - name: landuse_code
    type: discrete
    bounds: [1, 3]
    sets: [1, 2, 3]
```

### `series`

SWAT series describe how to extract simulation output from SWAT output files (`output.rch`, `output.sub`, `output.hru`).

```yaml
series:
  - id: flow
    sim:
      file: output.rch
      id: 62
      period: [2019, 2021]
      timestep: monthly
      colSpan: [50, 61]
    obs:
      file: obs_flow_monthly.txt
      rowRanges:
        - [1, 36]
      colSpan: [1, 12]
```

Key fields:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `sim.file` | SWAT output file (`output.rch`, `output.sub`, or `output.hru`) |
| `sim.id` | Reach/subbasin/HRU ID (1-based) |
| `sim.period` | Time window: `[2019, 2021]`, `["2019-06", "2020-09"]`, or multi-segment `[[2019, 2019], [2021, 2021]]` |
| `sim.timestep` | `daily`, `monthly`, or `yearly` — must match the SWAT project IPRINT setting |
| `sim.colSpan` | Column range `[start, end]` for the variable |
| `sim.variable` | Variable name from the SWAT variable database (resolves `colSpan` automatically when set) |
| `sim.rowRanges` | Write this directly instead of `id` + `period` to bypass row calculation |

When `variable` is used instead of `colSpan`, the template looks up the column range from the SWAT variable database:

```yaml
sim:
  file: output.rch
  id: 62
  period: [2019, 2021]
  timestep: monthly
  variable: FLOW_OUT
```

Observation files are referenced relative to the config file location:

```yaml
obs:
  file: obs_flow_monthly.txt
  rowRanges:
    - [1, 36]
  colSpan: [1, 12]
```

### `functions`, `derived`, `objectives`

Same structure as general mode:

```yaml
functions:
  - name: NSE
    kind: builtin

derived:
  - id: nse_flow
    call:
      func: NSE
      args: [flow.sim, flow.obs]

objectives:
  - id: obj_nse
    ref: nse_flow
    sense: max
```

## Project discovery

When the template loads, it reads the SWAT project directory to extract metadata:

| File | What is read |
|---|---|
| `file.cio` | Simulation period (start/end year, julian days), output timestep (IPRINT), output skip years (NYSKIP) |
| `fig.fig` | Subbasin count and IDs |
| `*.sub` | Subbasin area, latitude, elevation, HRU count, HRU file list |
| `*.hru` (header) | Land use, soil, slope class per HRU |

This metadata is used to:

- Calculate `rowRanges` for series extraction.
- Resolve HRU-level parameter file targets.
- Validate that `sim.id` values are within range.

## Available built-in functions

`NSE`, `KGE`, `R2`, `RMSE`, `MSE`, `PBIAS`, `LogNSE`, `sum_series`, plus external Python functions.

## Reference examples

- `examples/test_daily.yaml` — SWAT 2012 daily timestep, single objective (NSE).
- `examples/test_monthly.yaml` — SWAT 2012 monthly timestep, single objective (NSE).
- `examples/test_monthly_complex.yaml` — SWAT 2012 monthly, multi-objective with constraints and diagnostics.
- `examples/test_monthly_series.yaml` — SWAT 2012 monthly, multi-series (flow + TN).

For each example, the expanded general config is available as `<stem>_general.yaml` after a successful `load_config()` call.

## Boundary

- **SWAT 2012 only.** This template targets the SWAT 2012 file format (file.cio, fig.fig, .sub/.hru structure, fixed-width parameter files). For SWAT+, use the [SWAT+ template](swatplus.md).
- The template generates `writerType: fixed_width` and `readerType: text`. CSV-based SWAT workflows fall outside this template's scope.
